C_fork_ternary.label: the candidate: PrismML fork build, ternary Bonsai-2 (PTQ1_0)

sample_size_note: 3 games x 2 seeds x 3 arms. Directional only, not statistically powered. Each arm's two seeds per game are not independent draws of the game.

superseded_first_pass_of_this_version.note: A first full pass used one engine store shared by all three arms and no policy telemetry. It was discarded and rerun with one store per arm. Episode scores, call counts and token counts matched the rerun exactly for all 18 episodes (the runs are seeded), so the shared store did not change any result.

truncation_diagnosis.finding: Both. The live agent asks for thinking by default, so a 512-token cap is spent entirely in hidden reasoning and the answer stays empty (hypothesis b). Even with thinking off, a valid engine needs 2.5k-3.5k tokens, so 512 was also too small (hypothesis a).

live_agent_defaults.think_flag_ignored_by_prior_harness: v1 passed no_think_prefix='/no_think', but generate() applies that prefix only when think mode is off. Think mode is on by default, so the prefix was inert.

truncation_diagnosis.probe_prompt: cd82 seed 7491001 induction prompt, stock server, mandated model
truncation_diagnosis.stock_server_note: chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false works on the stock server (D2). The live agent's own switch CARNOT_ARC_INDUCE_THINK=0 was used instead, so no live code changed.

ternary_model_chat_endpoint_probes.finding: The ternary model also thinks by default (D1: answer channel empty at 512). On the chat endpoint with thinking off it writes a long, full engine (D2, hit the 4096 cap). On the raw code-only path that the think-off switch selects, it answered tersely and often omitted the engine function. So the low induction success of the ternary arm in this eval is partly a prompt-format effect of the raw path, not proof the weights cannot write the code. The chat path was probed once, not run through the 18-episode matrix.
